name: Sound Demixing Benchmarks (music source separation)
description: Music demixing is the task of separating different tracks from the given single audio signal into components, such as drums, bass, and vocals from the rest of the accompaniment. Separation of sources is useful for a range of areas, including entertainment and hearing aids. In this paper, we introduce two new benchmarks for the sound source separation tasks and compare popular models for sound demixing, as well as their ensembles, on these benchmarks. For the models' assessments, we provide the leaderboard at https://mvsep.com/quality_checker/, giving a comparison for a range of models. The new benchmark datasets are available for download. We also develop a novel approach for audio separation, based on the ensembling of different models that are suited best for the particular stem. The proposed solution was evaluated in the context of the Music Demixing Challenge 2023 and achieved top results in different tracks of the challenge. The code and the approach are open-sourced on GitHub.
evaluation_method: SI-SDR / SDR (standard source-separation objective metrics), with perceptual listening tests as supplementary evaluation
typical_sota_score: 8–15 dB (SI-SDR, varies by instrument/stem and track)
reputation: Widely used in the audio research community (including the Music Demixing Challenge) with an active leaderboard and strong adoption for benchmarking source-separation models.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; objective metrics (SI-SDR/SDR) do not fully capture perceptual quality. Multiple tracks and dataset splits exist; ensembles and task-specific tuning can inflate leaderboard performance. Licensing and dataset size vary by release.
